Light viewers (1 to 15 titles) convert at 0.49 (0.19 to 0.82) times their expected rate and heavy viewers (over 40 titles) at 1.48 (1.04 to 1.92), or 1.79 (1.12 to 2.50) among never-major donors. The direction holds in each validation cohort, with heavy viewers between 1.10 and 1.99 and light viewers between 0.24 and 0.69. However, each cohort has at most 11 converters per group, and at 3 years the pattern mostly fades (0.94 for light viewers and 1.14 for heavy viewers). Titles viewed is worth testing in the 12 month model, but it is a modest and uncertain signal.

Summary for Modeling

  • Solicitation adds no clear signal once prior-year giving is known. Responses are payments already counted in giving, and the solicitation counts partly reflect PBS Utah’s mailing decisions.
  • Having a Passport viewing record adds nothing either. The number of titles viewed shows a modest 12 month signal that should be tested in the model but not relied on.
  • The overall differences that some individual EDAs found for both sources come mostly from giving level, which explains most of the disagreement among them.
  • Outcome-year solicitations and responses must be excluded. Passport features should keep a “no viewing record” level, and viewing records rarely persist from year to year.
  • Neither source reaches back before FY2021, so the 5 year outcome, which needs earlier cohorts, has to do without them. This costs little.

Snapshot Fields and Leakage

The constituent table has one row per person, measured at the end of the data (FY2026). A field can only be a feature if its value at an earlier prediction date would have been the same, or if it can be rebuilt for that date. This section checks what each varying field encodes, tests the usable ones within giving bands, and collects the leakage rules from the whole notebook.

PBS Classification Fields

con = clean["constituents"]
people = con.filter(pl.col("primary_constituent_type") != "Organization")
fy26 = person_years.filter(pl.col("fy") == 2026)
status = (
    people.select("constituent_id", "major_donor_class_pbs_utah", "annual_giving_group", "sustainer_pbs_utah",
                  "lifetime_uofu_fundraising", "previous_fy_uofu_cash", "prospect_committed_giving_amount_uofu")
    .join(fy26.select("constituent_id", total_fy26="total", recurring_fy26="recurring_amt"), on="constituent_id", how="left")
    .join(person_years.filter(pl.col("fy") == 2025).select("constituent_id", total_fy25="total"), on="constituent_id", how="left")
    .join(person_years.group_by("constituent_id").agg(
              lifetime_pbs=pl.col("total").sum(),
              major_before_fy26=pl.col("major_individual").filter(pl.col("fy") < 2026).any()),
          on="constituent_id", how="left")
    .with_columns(pl.col("total_fy26", "recurring_fy26", "total_fy25", "lifetime_pbs").fill_null(0),
                  pl.col("major_before_fy26").fill_null(False))
)

class_decode = (
    status.group_by(major_donor_class=pl.col("major_donor_class_pbs_utah").fill_null("(blank)"))
    .agg(people=pl.len(), major_alone_in_fy26=(pl.col("total_fy26") >= 1200).mean(),
         major_before_fy26=pl.col("major_before_fy26").mean(),
         min_fy26_giving=pl.col("total_fy26").min(), max_fy26_giving=pl.col("total_fy26").max())
    .sort("people")
)
group_decode = (
    status.filter(pl.col("annual_giving_group").is_not_null())
    .group_by("annual_giving_group")
    .agg(people=pl.len(), gave_in_fy26=(pl.col("total_fy26") > 0).mean(),
         min_fy26_giving=pl.col("total_fy26").filter(pl.col("total_fy26") > 0).min(),
         max_fy26_giving=pl.col("total_fy26").max())
    .sort("min_fy26_giving", nulls_last=False)
)
cd = {r["major_donor_class"]: r for r in class_decode.iter_rows(named=True)}
sustainer_match = (status["sustainer_pbs_utah"] == (status["recurring_fy26"] > 0)).mean()

# how the snapshot classifies the couple that is major only in combination
couple_snapshot = (
    person_years.filter("major_combined_only")
    .join(con.select("constituent_id", "major_donor_class_pbs_utah", "annual_giving_group"), on="constituent_id")
)

show(class_decode, pct_cols=["major_alone_in_fy26", "major_before_fy26"], caption="Major donor class compared with FY2026 giving")
show(group_decode, pct_cols=["gave_in_fy26"], caption="Annual giving group compared with FY2026 giving")

All three PBS classifications describe FY2026 giving:

  • Major donor class. Broadcaster and Director are exactly the people who gave $1,200 or more on their own in FY2026, with Broadcasters at exactly $1,200 and Directors at $2,000 or more. Former means major in an earlier year but not in FY2026, and a blank means never major. The documented ranges ($1,000 to $4,999 for Broadcaster and $5,000 to $9,999 for Director) do not match the data.
  • Annual giving group. Its meaning is listed as unknown, but it lines up with FY2026 giving: ND is no gift in FY2026, and PD, LD, SL, and CD are increasing ranges, with CD starting at $1,200.
  • Sustainer flag. It matches “had recurring payments in FY2026” for 100.0% of people.

For any cohort before FY2025 these fields come from after the outcome year, and for the FY2025 cohort they are the outcome. All three are dropped. The earlier sections rebuild the same information for any year from the giving panel (former major status, monthly sustainer amount).

The snapshot also bears on the household rule. The 2 spouses who reach $1,200 only together in FY2026 have a blank major donor class, and each is in giving group SL on their own giving. In this data, PBS’s own classification counts major status per person without combining spouses. The team’s rule came from PBS’s description of how it counts households, so this is a point to confirm with PBS, although it affects only this one couple.

University of Utah Fields

The problem statement lists University of Utah capacity information as an input. The three UofU dollar fields were compared with each person’s PBS giving.

givers = status.filter(pl.col("lifetime_pbs") > 0)
cash_bands = (
    status.group_by("previous_fy_uofu_cash")
    .agg(people=pl.len(), min_fy25_giving=pl.col("total_fy25").min(), max_fy25_giving=pl.col("total_fy25").max())
    .sort("previous_fy_uofu_cash")
)
# do the FY2025 giving ranges of the cash codes overlap?
cash_ranges = cash_bands.filter(pl.col("previous_fy_uofu_cash") > 0).sort("min_fy25_giving")
cash_overlap = (cash_ranges["min_fy25_giving"].shift(-1) <= cash_ranges["max_fy25_giving"]).sum()

uofu_checks = pl.DataFrame([
    {"field": "Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "check": "correlation with lifetime PBS giving",
     "value": f'{givers.select(pl.corr("lifetime_uofu_fundraising", "lifetime_pbs")).item():.2f}'},
    {"field": "Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "check": "at least as large as lifetime PBS giving",
     "value": pct((givers["lifetime_uofu_fundraising"] >= givers["lifetime_pbs"]).mean())},
    {"field": "Previous FY UofU Cash", "check": "positive exactly when the person gave in FY2025",
     "value": pct(((status["previous_fy_uofu_cash"] > 0) == (status["total_fy25"] > 0)).mean())},
    {"field": "Previous FY UofU Cash", "check": "distinct values",
     "value": n(status["previous_fy_uofu_cash"].n_unique())},
    {"field": "Prospect Committed Giving UofU", "check": "positive exactly when the sustainer flag is set",
     "value": pct(((status["prospect_committed_giving_amount_uofu"] > 0) == status["sustainer_pbs_utah"]).mean())},
    {"field": "Prospect Committed Giving UofU", "check": "equal to FY2026 recurring giving",
     "value": pct((status["prospect_committed_giving_amount_uofu"] == status["recurring_fy26"]).mean())},
])
uc = {(r["field"], r["check"]): r["value"] for r in uofu_checks.iter_rows(named=True)}
show(uofu_checks, caption="How the UofU dollar fields relate to PBS giving")
show(cash_bands, caption="Previous FY UofU Cash values and the FY2025 PBS giving behind each")

None of the three is independent of PBS giving:

  • Lifetime UofU Fundraising has a correlation of 0.90 with lifetime PBS giving through FY2026 and is at least as large for 93.9% of donors, so it looks like a total that includes PBS giving.
  • Previous FY UofU Cash takes only 6 values, and each one matches a range of the person’s FY2025 PBS giving that does not overlap the others. It is a coded version of FY2025 PBS giving.
  • Prospect Committed Giving is positive exactly when the sustainer flag is set (100.0% agreement) and equals FY2026 recurring giving for 87.7% of people.
# how strong the lifetime field would look if it were used
feat_snap = feat12.join(
    con.select("constituent_id", "lifetime_uofu_fundraising", "age", "gender", "address_state",
               "primary_constituent_type", "spouse_constituent_id"),
    on="constituent_id", how="left",
)
leak_specs = [
    ("Lifetime UofU Fundraising", pl.col("lifetime_uofu_fundraising").cut([1000, 5000], labels=["$1,000 or less", "$1,001 to $5,000", "over $5,000"]).cast(pl.String),
     ["$1,000 or less", "$1,001 to $5,000", "over $5,000"]),
]
leak_signals = signal_table(feat_snap, leak_specs)
show(display_signals(leak_signals), pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="How strong lifetime UofU fundraising would look if used (it leaks the outcome)")

Used as a feature, the lifetime field would look as strong as former major status. Donors above $5,000 convert at 13.1%, 3.16 (2.77 to 3.64) times what their prior-year giving predicts, and 6.60 (4.94 to 8.93) times among never-major donors, the largest ratio for that group in the notebook. That strength comes from counting the outcome years. All three UofU fields are dropped, which leaves no measure of giving capacity outside PBS Utah.

Fields That Can Be Used

The remaining varying fields describe the person rather than their giving. Age is shifted back to the prediction date by subtracting the years between FY t and FY2026, assuming the snapshot age is as of FY2026. Gender, state, and having a spouse on file are assumed not to change. Constituent type is included here only as the sensitivity check the team agreed on, since it may be a label that changed over time.

feat_snap = feat_snap.with_columns(
    age_at_t=pl.col("age") - (2026 - pl.col("t")),
    type_group=pl.when(pl.col("primary_constituent_type").is_in(["Friends", "Donors"])).then(pl.col("primary_constituent_type"))
        .when(pl.col("primary_constituent_type").str.starts_with("Alumni")).then(pl.lit("Alumni"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("other University affiliation")),
)
AGE_LABELS = ["40 or under", "41 to 55", "56 to 70", "71 to 85", "over 85"]
demo_specs = [
    ("Age at prediction date", pl.col("age_at_t").cut([40, 55, 70, 85], labels=AGE_LABELS).cast(pl.String), AGE_LABELS),
    ("Gender", pl.col("gender").fill_null("Unknown"), ["Female", "Male", "Unknown"]),
    ("Lives in Utah", pl.when(pl.col("address_state") == "UT").then(pl.lit("yes")).otherwise(pl.lit("no")), ["no", "yes"]),
    ("Spouse on file", pl.when(pl.col("spouse_constituent_id").is_not_null()).then(pl.lit("yes")).otherwise(pl.lit("no")), ["no", "yes"]),
    ("Constituent type (sensitivity only)", pl.col("type_group"), ["Friends", "Donors", "Alumni", "other University affiliation"]),
]
demo_signals = signal_table(feat_snap, demo_specs)

def dci(feature, level, never=False):
    return ci(feature, level, never, tbl=demo_signals)

type_tenure = (
    feat_snap.group_by("type_group")
    .agg(median_years_since_first_gift=pl.col("years_since_first_gift").median(),
         first_gift_before_fy2021=(pl.col("t") - pl.col("years_since_first_gift") + 1 < 2021).mean())
)
tt = {r["type_group"]: r for r in type_tenure.iter_rows(named=True)}

show(display_signals(demo_signals), pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="Usable constituent fields within prior-year bands, 12 month outcome")
  • Age matters mainly at the young end. Donors 40 and under at the prediction date convert at 0.44 (0.22 to 0.70) times their expected rate (0.51 (0.20 to 0.89) for never-major donors). The older groups are near or slightly above 1, with intervals that include 1, and the never-major pattern across them is not steady.
  • Gender matters mainly through the Unknown group, at 0.56 (0.36 to 0.77). Unknown gender may mark thinner records, so it is kept as its own level.
  • State and spouse on file make little difference (1.02 (0.95 to 1.09) for Utah residents and 0.86 (0.54 to 1.22) for donors with a spouse on file).
  • Constituent type separates Friends (1.37 (1.22 to 1.53)) from Donors (0.65 (0.49 to 0.81)), but it also tracks giving history: 100% of Friends donor-years belong to people whose first gift came before FY2021, compared with 42% for Donors. It probably repeats the tenure and legacy features, which supports leaving it out of the main model and testing it only as a sensitivity check.

Leakage Rules

# soft credits in the outcome year among 12 month converters
conv12 = feat12.filter("converted").select("constituent_id", "t", "soft_in_t", "soft_before")
outcome_soft = conv12.join(person_years.select("constituent_id", t=pl.col("fy") - 1, soft_outcome=pl.col("soft_amt") > 0),
                           on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left").with_columns(pl.col("soft_outcome").fill_null(False))
soft_in_outcome = outcome_soft["soft_outcome"].mean()
soft_first_in_outcome = (outcome_soft["soft_outcome"] & ~outcome_soft["soft_in_t"] & ~outcome_soft["soft_before"]).mean()

Soft credits are the clearest case of timing leakage in the giving data. 98.4% of 12 month converters have a soft credit in the year they become major, and for 45.0% it is their first soft credit. Lifetime soft credit counts would therefore look very strong if they were not cut off at FY t. The table collects every leakage rule in this notebook.

Leakage rules for a FY t snapshot
Source Rule for a FY t snapshot Reason
Major donor class, annual giving group, sustainer flag Dropped Rebuilt from FY2026 giving
UofU lifetime fundraising, previous FY cash, committed giving Dropped Include or code PBS giving through FY2025 or FY2026
Payments, soft credits, legacy gifts, gift types Gifts dated on or before June 30 of FY t Outcome-year gifts are the outcome, and most converters receive a soft credit in the conversion year
Solicitations and responses FY t and earlier Converters are solicited less in the outcome year, and responses are outcome-year payments
Passport viewing FY t and earlier Outcome-year viewing is not known at the prediction date
Age Shifted to FY t The snapshot age is measured in FY2026
Cultivation selection and contact Covered in the next section Officers select donors partly on the information the model would use

Summary for Modeling

  • Drop: major donor class, annual giving group, the sustainer flag, and all three UofU dollar fields. Each is built from PBS giving through FY2025 or FY2026.
  • Use: age shifted to the prediction date, which mainly flags younger donors, and gender with Unknown as its own level. State and spouse on file can be included but add little.
  • Sensitivity only: constituent type, which largely repeats giving history.
  • No outside capacity measure is available, so the model has to rely on PBS giving history. The business problem statement should say so.
  • Household rule: the snapshot classification does not combine spouses, which should be confirmed with PBS.

Cultivation Program

From FY2022 to FY2025, each of eight officer portfolios selected 125 donors a year. Within each portfolio, about three quarters of the selected donors were contacted and the rest were randomly held out. Portfolios also adopted a cultivation program at different times. Contact may change who becomes a major donor, which affects the outcome the model learns from, and the random holdout gives a fair way to measure that effect. Following decision 8, this section measures the effect and sets how contacted donors are handled. It does not build an uplift or operational model.

How the Program Was Run

cult = (
    clean["cultivation"].rename({"synthetic_id": "constituent_id", "fiscal_year": "t"})
    .join(clean["portfolios"].select("portfolio_id", "rollout_fy"), on="portfolio_id", how="left")
)
cult_summary = (
    cult.group_by("t")
    .agg(selected=pl.len(), contacted=pl.col("contacted").sum(), held_out=pl.col("holdout").sum(),
         in_adopting_portfolios=pl.col("program_adopted").sum())
    .sort("t")
)
adoption_matches_rollout = (cult["program_adopted"] == (cult["t"] >= cult["rollout_fy"].fill_null(9999))).mean()
selected_people = cult["constituent_id"].n_unique()

# the assignment year lines up with cohort t: selected donors gave in FY t and were not major
cult_year = cult.join(person_years.select("constituent_id", t=pl.col("fy"), total_t=pl.col("total"), major_t=pl.col("major")),
                      on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left")
gave_in_assignment_year = (cult_year["total_t"].fill_null(0) > 0).mean()
major_in_assignment_year = cult_year["major_t"].fill_null(False).mean()

show(cult_summary, caption="Cultivation selections, contacts, and holdouts by year")

Each year 1,000 donors were selected, and program adoption follows the rollout year in the portfolio table exactly (100.0% agreement): two portfolios adopted in FY2023, two in FY2024, two in FY2025, one in FY2026 after the program window, and one never. Over the four years 2,398 different people were selected. 100.0% of selected donors gave in their assignment year and 0.0% were major that year, so a donor assigned in FY t is an eligible donor at the end of FY t, and the outcome is whether they become major in FY t+1. Each assignment year is matched to the cohort with the same t.

Who Gets Selected

feat_cult = with_features(active.filter((pl.col("window") == 1) & pl.col("t").is_between(2022, 2025))).join(
    cult.select("constituent_id", "t", "contacted", "program_adopted"), on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="left"
).with_columns(
    group=pl.when(pl.col("contacted").is_null()).then(pl.lit("not selected"))
        .when(pl.col("contacted")).then(pl.lit("selected, contacted")).otherwise(pl.lit("selected, held out")),
    prior_rank=pl.col("prior_total").rank(descending=True).over("t") / pl.len().over("t"),
)
selected_in_eligible = cult.join(feat_cult.select("constituent_id", "t"), on=["constituent_id", "t"], how="semi").height / cult.height
selected_share = feat_cult["contacted"].is_not_null().mean()
median_rank_selected = feat_cult.filter(pl.col("contacted").is_not_null())["prior_rank"].median()

selection_profile = (
    feat_cult.group_by("group")
    .agg(donor_years=pl.len(), median_prior_year_giving=pl.col("prior_total").median(),
         former_major=pl.col("former_major").mean(), gave_5_of_5_years=(pl.col("years_last5") == 5).mean(),
         soft_credit_before=pl.col("soft_before").mean(), converted_next_year=pl.col("converted").mean())
    .sort("group")
)
show(selection_profile, pct_cols=["former_major", "gave_5_of_5_years", "soft_credit_before", "converted_next_year"], pct_digits=2, caption="Selected, held-out, and non-selected donors compared, FY2022 to FY2025 cohorts")

Selection draws from the eligible population (100.0% of selected donors are eligible in their cohort) and covers about 3.1% of it each year. Officers pick from the top of the giving distribution: the median selected donor ranks in the top 4.0% of eligible donors by prior-year giving. Selected donors are also more often former major donors, consistent givers, and past soft credit recipients. The contacted and held-out groups look alike on every measure, as random assignment should produce.

The within-band test shows whether officers see more than prior-year giving. Contacted donors are left out, because contact raised their conversion and would inflate the band rates. That leaves the held-out donors, who were selected the same way but never contacted, and the donors who were not selected. The table uses the FY2022 to FY2024 cohorts.

cult_val = feat_cult.filter(pl.col("in_validation"))
uncontacted = cult_val.filter(pl.col("group") != "selected, contacted")
cult_specs = [("Cultivation group", pl.col("group"), ["not selected", "selected, held out"])]
cult_signals = signal_table(uncontacted, cult_specs)
held_top_band = uncontacted.filter(pl.col("group") == "selected, held out")["band"].is_in(["$241 to $500", "over $500"]).mean()
show(display_signals(cult_signals), pct_cols=["rate"], pct_digits=3, caption="Held-out compared with non-selected donors within prior-year bands, contacted donors left out")

Among donors who were not contacted, held-out donors convert at 2.72 (1.67 to 4.08) times the rate their prior-year giving predicts, so officers select on more than giving level even before contact. Among never-major donors the ratio is 1.99 (0.37 to 3.98), with an interval that includes 1, so part of what officers see may be former major status. Selection also leans on giving: 52% of held-out donor-years gave more than $240 in FY t, compared with 6.8% of all eligible donor-years. Officer selection is therefore a demanding benchmark for the model, which the baselines section measures directly.

Effect of Contact

The held-out donors were selected the same way as the contacted donors, so the difference in their conversion rates estimates what contact itself does. Intervals use the couple-clustered bootstrap. Following decision 9, the main estimates use the FY2022 to FY2024 cohorts, and the FY2025 cohort, whose outcomes fall in FY2026, is shown once on its own.

def clustered_diff(df, reps=1000, seed=20261009):
    # contacted minus held-out conversion rate, resampling couples with replacement
    g = df.group_by("couple_id").agg(
        n1=pl.col("contacted").sum(), c1=(pl.col("contacted") & pl.col("converted")).sum(),
        n0=(~pl.col("contacted")).sum(), c0=(~pl.col("contacted") & pl.col("converted")).sum(),
    ).sort("couple_id")
    n1, c1, n0, c0 = (g[c].to_numpy() for c in ("n1", "c1", "n0", "c0"))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    m = len(g)
    draws = np.empty(reps)
    for r in range(reps):
        k = rng.integers(0, m, m)
        draws[r] = c1[k].sum() / n1[k].sum() - c0[k].sum() / n0[k].sum()
    return c1.sum() / n1.sum(), c0.sum() / n0.sum(), np.quantile(draws, 0.025), np.quantile(draws, 0.975), int(n1.sum()), int(n0.sum())

selected = feat_cult.filter(pl.col("contacted").is_not_null())
sel_val = selected.filter("in_validation")
effect_specs = [
    ("all selected donors", "FY2022 to FY2024", sel_val),
    ("before program adoption", "FY2022 to FY2024", sel_val.filter(~pl.col("program_adopted"))),
    ("after program adoption", "FY2022 to FY2024", sel_val.filter(pl.col("program_adopted"))),
    ("never-major donors", "FY2022 to FY2024", sel_val.filter(~pl.col("former_major"))),
    ("all selected donors (labeled check)", "FY2025", selected.filter(pl.col("t") == 2025)),
]
effect_rows = []
for group, cohorts_used, df in effect_specs:
    p1, p0, lo, hi, n1_, n0_ = clustered_diff(df)
    effect_rows.append({"group": group, "cohorts": cohorts_used, "contacted": n1_, "contacted_rate": p1,
                        "held_out": n0_, "held_out_rate": p0, "difference": p1 - p0, "ci_low": lo, "ci_high": hi})
effects = pl.DataFrame(effect_rows)
eff = {r["group"]: r for r in effects.iter_rows(named=True)}
show(effects, pct_cols=["contacted_rate", "held_out_rate", "difference", "ci_low", "ci_high"], pct_digits=2, caption="Contacted minus held-out conversion, with couple-clustered 95% intervals")
e_all, e_before, e_after = eff["all selected donors"], eff["before program adoption"], eff["after program adoption"]
e_never, e_25 = eff["never-major donors"], eff["all selected donors (labeled check)"]
# describe where the before-adoption interval sits relative to zero
before_zero_text = ("just touching zero" if abs(e_before["ci_low"]) < 0.0005
                    else "including zero" if e_before["ci_low"] < 0 else "excluding zero")

Contact raises conversion. Across the FY2022 to FY2024 cohorts, contacted donors convert at 4.17% and held-out donors at 2.02%, a difference of 2.15 percentage points (95% interval 0.81 to 3.48). Following Kate’s EDA, the table splits the effect by whether the portfolio had adopted the program. Before adoption the difference is 1.46 points (-0.12 to 2.94, including zero), and after adoption it is 4.23 points (1.33 to 7.02), from only 750 donor-years. Among never-major donors the difference is 1.03 points (0.22 to 1.77). In the FY2025 cohort, contacted donors converted at 7.46% and held-out donors at 3.63%. The held-out rate in that cohort is higher than in any earlier one, and since those donors were never contacted, part of the FY2026 rise comes from donors themselves, which the next section examines.

How Much Conversion Runs Through the Program

def program_share(t):
    # new major donors in FY t+1 (major in t+1, not in t) and whether they were selected or contacted in FY t
    new_next = (
        person_years.filter((pl.col("fy") == t + 1) & pl.col("major")).select("constituent_id")
        .join(person_years.filter((pl.col("fy") == t) & pl.col("major")), on="constituent_id", how="anti")
    )
    sel_t = cult.filter(pl.col("t") == t)
    return {"cohort": t, "new_majors_next_year": new_next.height,
            "selected_in_fy_t": new_next.join(sel_t, on="constituent_id", how="semi").height,
            "contacted_in_fy_t": new_next.join(sel_t.filter("contacted"), on="constituent_id", how="semi").height}

program_shares = pl.DataFrame([program_share(t) for t in range(2022, 2026)])
ps_val = program_shares.filter(pl.col("cohort") <= 2024).select(pl.exclude("cohort").sum()).row(0, named=True)
contacted_conv_share = cult_val.filter(pl.col("group") == "selected, contacted")["converted"].sum() / cult_val["converted"].sum()
contact_attrib = ps_val["contacted_in_fy_t"] * (1 - e_all["held_out_rate"] / e_all["contacted_rate"])
show(program_shares, caption="New major donors who were selected or contacted the year before")

Of the 153 new major donors in FY2023 to FY2025, 109 (71.2%) had been selected the year before and 94 had been contacted. Using the held-out rate as what would have happened without contact, roughly 49 of those contacted conversions can be credited to contact. This is a rough figure, but it means part of the outcome in these years was produced by staff action.

Handling Contacted Donors

For FY2022 to FY2024, contacted donors include 70% of all 12 month converters, so dropping them would remove a large share of the positive cases. Following decision 8:

  • Training only. Two flags, contacted in FY t and selected but held out in FY t, are added in training so the model can separate the effect of contact from donor potential.
  • Scoring. Every donor is scored with both flags off, so lists rank donors on their own potential.
  • Reporting. Results are reported for all eligible donors and for donors who were not contacted, since contact inflates the measured recall of any ranking for the FY2022 to FY2025 cohorts.
  • Officer benchmark. Officer selection is compared with the model on held-out donors only, where contact has not changed the outcome.

Summary for Modeling

  • Officers select about 3% of eligible donors a year, and held-out donors convert well above what their giving predicts, so officer selection is a strong benchmark. For never-major donors this is less certain.
  • Contact raises conversion by about 2.2 percentage points across the validation cohorts. The effect looks larger after program adoption, as Kate found, but the after-adoption estimate rests on only 750 donor-years.
  • Part of the outcome in FY2023 to FY2025 comes from contact, so contact flags are used in training only and results are also reported for donors who were not contacted.

The FY2026 Influx

Federal funding for public broadcasting ended in 2025, and FY2026 (July 2025 to June 2026) is the first full year after the cut. The business problem names the resulting influx of donations as a risk, because the last year may not look like the years a model learns from. This section describes what changed in FY2026, separates the donors’ own response from the cultivation program, and checks the decision to keep the FY2025 cohort, whose outcomes fall in FY2026, out of validation.

What Changed in FY2026

first_gift = person_years.group_by("constituent_id").agg(first_fy=pl.col("fy").min())
donor_kind = (
    person_years.filter(pl.col("fy") >= 2020).select("constituent_id", "fy", "total")
    .join(first_gift, on="constituent_id")
    .sort("constituent_id", "fy")
    .with_columns(prev_fy=pl.col("fy").shift(1).over("constituent_id"), prev_total=pl.col("total").shift(1).over("constituent_id"))
    .filter(pl.col("fy") >= 2021)
    .with_columns(kind=pl.when(pl.col("first_fy") == pl.col("fy")).then(pl.lit("first gift"))
                  .when(pl.col("prev_fy") == pl.col("fy") - 1).then(pl.lit("gave last year"))
                  .otherwise(pl.lit("returning after a gap")))
)
kind_by_year = (
    donor_kind.group_by("fy").agg(
        first_gift=(pl.col("kind") == "first gift").sum(),

)

    .agg(retained_donors=pl.len(), gave_more=(pl.col("total") > pl.col("prev_total")).mean(),

kb = {r["fy"]: r for r in kind_by_year.iter_rows(named=True)}
rt = {r["fy"]: r for r in retained.iter_rows(named=True)}
rt_before = retained.filter(pl.col("fy") < 2026)

The influx shows up in three places:

  • First-time donors nearly doubled, from 4,530 in FY2025 to 8,801 in FY2026. Their median first-year giving stayed at $60, the same as in every earlier year, so these are more donors of the usual size rather than larger gifts.
  • Returning donors gave more. Among donors who also gave the year before, 26.0% increased their giving in FY2026, compared with 17.7% to 20.2% in earlier years, and their net change was $245,946 after being negative in every earlier Unite year.
  • More lapsed donors came back: 3,323 in FY2026, up from 2,610.

Conversion in FY2026

The FY2025 cohort is the one whose 12 month outcome falls in FY2026. It is also the cohort with the most portfolios using the cultivation program, so a rise in conversion could come from either source. The held-out donors separate the two, since they were selected but never contacted.

The FY2025 cohort converted at 0.246% (95% interval 0.192% to 0.298%), compared with 0.111% to 0.178% for the four earlier cohorts. Contacted donors converted at 7.46%, compared with 3.59% to 4.52% before, and held-out donors, who were never contacted, at 3.63%, compared with 1.61% to 2.42%. The held-out rise cannot come from contact, which suggests that part of the FY2026 jump is donors’ own response to the funding cut. The evidence is thin, though: the held-out group has about 250 donors a year and 9 converters in FY2025, and donors who were not selected converted at 0.050%, essentially the same as the FY2022 cohort (0.050%) and within about the earlier range (0.013% to 0.050%).

Who Converted in FY2026

A higher rate is a problem for validation mainly if it comes with a change in who converts. The table compares the converters in the FY2025 cohort with those in the four validation cohorts.

The mix of converters shifted. In the FY2025 cohort, 45.7% of converters are former major donors (53.4% before), 53.1% gave more than $500 in FY t (67.7% before), and 51.9% reached $2,000 or more (37.0% before). With 81 converters these differences are uncertain, but they point the same way: after the cut, more conversions came from donors lower in the giving range, and more converters went straight to $2,000 or more.

def top_k_recall(df, col, k):
    # expected recall in the top k by col, with ties at the cutoff split evenly
    df = df.sort(col, descending=True)
    total = df["converted"].sum()
    if total == 0 or k >= df.height:
        return None
    cut = df[col][k - 1]
    above = df.filter(pl.col(col) > cut)
    tied = df.filter(pl.col(col) == cut)
    return (above["converted"].sum() + tied["converted"].sum() * (k - above.height) / tied.height) / total

ranking_rows = []
for t in range(2021, 2026):
    d = active12.filter(pl.col("t") == t)
    ranking_rows.append({"cohort": t, "converters": int(d["converted"].sum()),
                         "recall_top_1000": top_k_recall(d, "prior_total", 1000),
                         "never_major_recall_top_1000": top_k_recall(d.filter(~pl.col("former_major")), "prior_total", 1000)})
ranking_by_cohort = pl.DataFrame(ranking_rows)
rk = {r["cohort"]: r for r in ranking_by_cohort.iter_rows(named=True)}
rk_before = ranking_by_cohort.filter(pl.col("cohort") < 2025)
show(ranking_by_cohort, pct_cols=["recall_top_1000", "never_major_recall_top_1000"], caption="Recall at 1,000 for the prior-year ranking, by cohort")

Ranking donors by prior-year giving, the baseline the model has to beat, finds 69.2% of FY2025 converters in the top 1,000, at the low end of the earlier cohorts (69.1% to 83.4%). So the influx raised the level of conversion and shifted the mix somewhat, but the simple ranking still works about as well. Both points support decision 9. The FY2025 cohort adds converters for final training, but its higher base rate and different mix would distort comparisons between models.

The Next List

fy26_eligible = person_years.filter((pl.col("fy") == 2026) & ~pl.col("major")).join(first_gift, on="constituent_id")
fy26_first_year_share = (fy26_eligible["first_fy"] == 2026).mean()
earlier_first_year_share = (
    person_years.filter(pl.col("fy").is_between(2021, 2025) & ~pl.col("major")).join(first_gift, on="constituent_id")
    .select((pl.col("first_fy") == pl.col("fy")).mean()).item()
)

The FY2026 cohort is the one PBS Utah would score next. 23.0% of its eligible donors made their first gift in FY2026, compared with 17.0% across the earlier cohorts. First-year donors converted at about a fifth of the rate their giving predicts (giving history section), so the influx makes the next eligible pool larger without adding many likely converters. That holds unless donors who joined because of the funding cut behave differently, which the data cannot show yet.

Summary for Modeling

  • FY2026 brought more first-time donors, more returning donors, and higher giving from existing donors.
  • Conversion rose among held-out donors who were never contacted, which suggests the rise is partly the donors’ own response to the funding cut, although the evidence rests on few converters.
  • The influx raised the conversion rate and shifted converters toward donors lower in the giving range, but the prior-year ranking still works about as well. The FY2025 cohort is used in final training and reported once as a labeled check, not for model selection (decision 9).
  • The next list will contain an unusually large share of first-year donors, whose behavior after the cut is untested.

Baselines

The model has to show that it finds future major donors better than simple rules PBS Utah could already use. Following decision 10, every baseline is scored the same way: each validation cohort is ranked, the top 1,000 donors form the list (about what the cultivation program can work in a year), and we report the share of converters on the list (recall), the share of the list that converts (precision), and precision divided by the base rate (lift). Ties at the cutoff are split evenly, so a rule that picks fewer than 1,000 donors fills the rest of the list at random. Results are pooled over the FY2021 to FY2024 cohorts, with couple-clustered intervals.

The baselines are:

  • Prior-year giving: donors ranked by their FY t giving. This is the bar to beat.
  • Recency, frequency, and value (RFV): the classic score named in the business problem, the sum of three 1 to 5 scores: days since the last gift (quintiles within the cohort, most recent = 5), years given in the last five, and FY t giving (quintiles).
  • Threshold rules from Erin’s EDA: gave $500 or more in FY t, and gave $1,000 or more over FY t-2 to FY t.
  • Former major or $500: a rule that adds the strongest signal from the giving history section to the first threshold.
  • Officer selection: the donors officers chose, measured only where contact has not changed the outcome (explained below).
def quintile(col, descending=False):
    # 1 to 5 score from the within-cohort percentile rank, with ties sharing a rank
    pct_rank = pl.col(col).rank("average", descending=descending) / pl.len()
    return (pct_rank * 5).ceil().clip(1, 5).cast(pl.Int32).over("t")

def add_scores(df):
    return df.with_columns(
        rfv=quintile("days_since_last_gift", descending=True) + pl.col("years_last5").cast(pl.Int32) + quintile("prior_total"),
        rule_500=(pl.col("prior_total") >= 500).cast(pl.Int32),
        rule_3yr_1000=((pl.col("prior_total") + pl.col("two_years_before")) >= 1000).cast(pl.Int32),
        rule_former_or_500=(pl.col("former_major") | (pl.col("prior_total") >= 500)).cast(pl.Int32),
    )

BASELINES = {
    "prior-year giving": "prior_total",
    "RFV score": "rfv",
    "rule: $500 or more in FY t": "rule_500",
    "rule: $1,000 or more over three years": "rule_3yr_1000",
    "rule: former major or $500 or more": "rule_former_or_500",
}
K = 1000

def ranked(df, col):
    # per cohort, rows sorted by score with a group id for each tied score
    parts = []
    for t in sorted(df["t"].unique().to_list()):
        d = df.filter(pl.col("t") == t).sort(col, descending=True)
        gid = (d[col].rank("dense", descending=True) - 1).cast(pl.Int64).to_numpy()
        parts.append((d["couple_id"], d["converted"].to_numpy().astype(float), d["w"].to_numpy().astype(float), gid))
    return parts

def hits_at_k(conv, w, gid, k):
    # expected converters in the top k by weight, splitting the tied group at the cutoff evenly
    gw = np.bincount(gid, weights=w)
    gc = np.bincount(gid, weights=w * conv)
    cum = np.cumsum(gw)
    g = np.searchsorted(cum, k)
    if g >= len(gw):
        return gc.sum()
    return gc[:g].sum() + gc[g] * (k - (cum[g] - gw[g])) / gw[g]

def evaluate(df, scores, k=K, reps=1000, seed=20261009):
    # pooled recall, precision, and lift at k with couple-clustered bootstrap intervals
    couples = df["couple_id"].unique().sort()
    lists = {name: [(couples.search_sorted(c).to_numpy(), conv, w, gid) for c, conv, w, gid in ranked(df, col)]
             for name, col in scores.items()}
    n_cohorts = df["t"].n_unique()

    def metrics(mult):
        out = {}
        for name, parts in lists.items():
            hits = conv_total = weight_total = 0.0
            for ci_, conv, w, gid in parts:
                ww = w if mult is None else w * mult[ci_]
                hits += hits_at_k(conv, ww, gid, k)
                conv_total += (ww * conv).sum()
                weight_total += ww.sum()
            precision = hits / (k * n_cohorts)
            out[name] = (hits / conv_total, precision, precision / (conv_total / weight_total))
        return out

    point = metrics(None)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    m = len(couples)
    draws = {name: [] for name in scores}
    for _ in range(reps):
        mult = np.bincount(rng.integers(0, m, m), minlength=m).astype(float)
        for name, vals in metrics(mult).items():
            draws[name].append(vals)
    rows = []
    for name in scores:
        d = np.array(draws[name])
        lo, hi = np.quantile(d, [0.025, 0.975], axis=0)
        r, p, l = point[name]
        rows.append({"baseline": name, "recall": r, "recall_low": lo[0], "recall_high": hi[0],
                     "precision": p, "lift": round(l, 1), "lift_low": round(lo[2], 1), "lift_high": round(hi[2], 1)})
    return pl.DataFrame(rows)

scored12 = add_scores(feat12).with_columns(w=pl.lit(1.0))

Baselines on the Validation Cohorts

base_all = evaluate(scored12, BASELINES)
base_never = evaluate(scored12.filter(~pl.col("former_major")), BASELINES)
random_recall = (K * scored12["t"].n_unique()) / scored12.height
random_recall_never = (K * scored12["t"].n_unique()) / scored12.filter(~pl.col("former_major")).height

baseline_table = pl.concat([
    base_all.with_columns(group=pl.lit("all eligible")),
    base_never.with_columns(group=pl.lit("never major")),
]).select("group", "baseline", "recall", "recall_low", "recall_high", "precision", "lift", "lift_low", "lift_high")
ba = {r["baseline"]: r for r in base_all.iter_rows(named=True)}
bn = {r["baseline"]: r for r in base_never.iter_rows(named=True)}
rule_500_size = scored12.group_by("t").agg(pl.col("rule_500").sum())["rule_500"].mean()
show(baseline_table, pct_cols=["recall", "recall_low", "recall_high", "precision"], caption="Baselines at a list of 1,000, FY2021 to FY2024 cohorts")
baseline_pd = baseline_table.with_columns(
    baseline=pl.col("baseline").str.replace_all("$", r"\$", literal=True),
    group=pl.col("group").str.slice(0, 1).str.to_uppercase() + pl.col("group").str.slice(1),
).to_pandas()
baseline_order = [b.replace("$", r"\$") for b in list(BASELINES)][::-1]
baseline_pd["baseline"] = pd.Categorical(baseline_pd["baseline"], categories=baseline_order, ordered=True)

(
    ggplot(baseline_pd, aes("baseline", "recall", color="group"))
    + geom_pointrange(aes(ymin="recall_low", ymax="recall_high"), position=position_dodge(width=0.5), size=0.5)
    + coord_flip()
    + scale_y_continuous(labels=percent_labels, limits=(0, 1))
    + labs(x="", y="Share of converters in the top 1,000 (recall)", color="",
           title="Prior-year giving is the bar to beat",
           subtitle="12 month outcome, FY2021 to FY2024 cohorts, 95% intervals")
    + theme(legend_position="top")
)

A random list of 1,000 would hold about 3.1% of converters. Ranking by prior-year giving holds 75.0% (95% interval 69.5% to 80.3%), with a precision of 3.55%, about 24 times the base rate. Among never-major donors it holds 59.5%. The other baselines compare as follows:

  • RFV is clearly weaker, at 39.5% overall and 29.6% for never-major donors. Its value quintile lumps together everyone in the top fifth of giving, and its recency part rewards monthly sustainers, who convert less than their giving predicts (giving history section).
  • The $500 rule reaches 68.5%. It picks about 279 donors a year and fills the rest of the list at random, while the prior-year ranking fills those places from the $241 to $500 band, which explains most of the gap. The three-year rule reaches 65.9%.
  • Former major or $500 reaches 76.1%, the same as the prior-year ranking within the uncertainty. For never-major donors the former major part has no effect, so it matches the $500 rule.

Officer Selection Without Contact

Officers chose about 1,000 donors a year from FY2022 to FY2024, but contact raised the conversion of the three quarters who were contacted, so their observed outcomes would flatter both officer selection and any ranking that puts them near the top. The held-out donors are a random quarter of the officers’ choices. Dropping the contacted donors and counting each held-out donor 4.03 times (1,000 selected over 248 held out) rebuilds the eligible pool as it would have looked without contact. All baselines, including officer selection, are scored on that pool.

held_weight = (
    cult.filter(pl.col("t").is_between(2022, 2024)).group_by("t")
    .agg(w_held=pl.len() / pl.col("holdout").sum())
)
no_contact = (
    add_scores(feat_cult.filter(pl.col("in_validation")))
    .filter(pl.col("group") != "selected, contacted")
    .join(held_weight, on="t", how="left")
    .with_columns(
        w=pl.when(pl.col("group") == "selected, held out").then(pl.col("w_held")).otherwise(pl.lit(1.0)),
        officer=(pl.col("group") == "selected, held out").cast(pl.Int32),
    )
)
NO_CONTACT_BASELINES = {"officer selection": "officer", **BASELINES}
base_nc = evaluate(no_contact, NO_CONTACT_BASELINES)
base_nc_never = evaluate(no_contact.filter(~pl.col("former_major")), NO_CONTACT_BASELINES)
nc_table = pl.concat([
    base_nc.with_columns(group=pl.lit("all eligible")),
    base_nc_never.with_columns(group=pl.lit("never major")),
]).select("group", "baseline", "recall", "recall_low", "recall_high", "precision", "lift", "lift_low", "lift_high")
nc = {r["baseline"]: r for r in base_nc.iter_rows(named=True)}
ncn = {r["baseline"]: r for r in base_nc_never.iter_rows(named=True)}
show(nc_table, pct_cols=["recall", "recall_low", "recall_high", "precision"], caption="Baselines on the no-contact pool, including officer selection, FY2022 to FY2024 cohorts")

Without contact, officer selection holds 70.8% of converters (52.4% to 80.7%), compared with 72.2% for the prior-year ranking and 74.7% for the former major or $500 rule. Among never-major donors the figures are 42.5%, 61.0%, and 43.6%. The intervals for officer selection are wide because they rest on the 744 held-out donor-years. Overall, officers do about as well as the prior-year ranking, so a model that beats the ranking would also be competitive with current practice. Among never-major donors officers appear to do worse than the ranking, but the intervals overlap widely and officers may be choosing donors for reasons other than conversion within a year.

Longer Outcome Windows

The 3 year outcome can be tested on the FY2021 and FY2022 cohorts. The 5 year outcome needs cohorts from FY2020 or earlier, before solicitation and Passport data begin, so it is tested with giving history only on the FY2011 to FY2020 cohorts.

LONG_BASELINES = {k: BASELINES[k] for k in ("prior-year giving", "RFV score", "rule: former major or $500 or more")}
scored3 = add_scores(feat3).with_columns(w=pl.lit(1.0))
c5 = cohorts.filter((pl.col("segment") == "active") & (pl.col("window") == 5) & pl.col("t").is_between(2011, 2020))
scored5 = add_scores(with_features(c5)).with_columns(w=pl.lit(1.0))
long_table = pl.concat([
    evaluate(scored3, LONG_BASELINES).with_columns(outcome=pl.lit("within 3 years"), cohorts=pl.lit("FY2021 to FY2022")),
    evaluate(scored5, LONG_BASELINES).with_columns(outcome=pl.lit("within 5 years"), cohorts=pl.lit("FY2011 to FY2020")),
]).select("outcome", "cohorts", "baseline", "recall", "recall_low", "recall_high", "precision", "lift")
lt = {(r["outcome"], r["baseline"]): r for r in long_table.iter_rows(named=True)}
show(long_table, pct_cols=["recall", "recall_low", "recall_high", "precision"], caption="Baselines for the 3 and 5 year outcomes")

The prior-year ranking holds 58.8% of 3 year converters and 55.8% of 5 year converters in the top 1,000. Recall falls as the window lengthens, so more of the eventual converters sit outside the top of the giving range, which leaves more room for a model to improve on the simple ranking. The former major or $500 rule does slightly better than the ranking at 3 years (61.8%) but worse at 5 years (47.1%). The 5 year cohorts come from the legacy years, when giving was recorded in a different system, so they show whether giving history alone carries over a long window rather than how a current model would perform.

Summary for Modeling

  • The bar to beat at a list of 1,000 is the prior-year ranking: 75.0% recall for all eligible donors and 59.5% for never-major donors over the FY2021 to FY2024 cohorts.
  • The classic RFV score is much weaker and should be reported but not used as the main comparison.
  • Simple threshold rules come close to the prior-year ranking, and the former major or $500 rule matches it at 12 months, which shows how much of the signal sits in giving level and former major status alone. The team agreed to keep the prior-year ranking as the main bar and to report the former major or $500 rule as a second check the model should also clear.
  • Officer selection is compared on the no-contact pool, where it holds 70.8% of converters against 72.2% for the prior-year ranking, with wide intervals.
  • The model’s room to add value is largest for never-major donors and for the longer windows.

Key Findings

This section pulls the results of the notebook together. The next section turns them into a plan for modeling.

Data Problems and How They Were Handled

  • Copy rows. 36,044 Unite payments ($447,530), 192 soft credits, and 216,128 legacy rows were copies of valid rows. Content-based rules removed them, and the copy labels agree with the rules exactly (0 mismatches).
  • Double counting through organizations. Organization payments equal the soft credits they fund in every year, so individual giving counts soft credits and leaves organization payments out.
  • Fields that describe the outcome. Major donor class, annual giving group, the sustainer flag, and all three University of Utah dollar fields reflect PBS giving through FY2025 or FY2026. All are dropped, which leaves no outside measure of giving capacity.
  • Missing Passport years. 50% of eligible donor-years have no viewing record, and only 34% to 41% of a year’s viewers appear the next year. Missing years are kept as their own level.
  • Staff action in the outcome. Among donors officers selected, contact raised conversion by 2.15 percentage points, so part of the outcome in FY2023 to FY2025 was produced by officers.
  • The FY2026 influx. The FY2025 cohort converted at 0.246% against 0.111% to 0.178% before, with a different mix of converters.
  • A definition to confirm. PBS Utah’s own classification counts the one couple that reaches $1,200 only in combination as two non-major donors, unlike the team’s household rule.

Strongest Relationships With the Target

  • Prior-year giving dominates. Donors who gave more than $500 in FY t convert at 11.5% and supply 68% of converters while being under 1% of eligible donor-years.
  • Former major status. Across the FY2021 to FY2025 cohorts, former major donors are 0.6% of eligible donor-years but 51% of converters, and they convert at 3.2 times what their giving predicts.
  • Length of giving history. First-year donors and donors with no gift the year before convert at about a fifth of what their giving predicts.
  • Officer judgment. Donors officers selected but never contacted convert at 2.7 times what their giving predicts, so officers see something beyond giving level.
  • Weak once giving is known: upgrade gifts, soft credits in FY t, solicitation volume and responses, communication channel, having a Passport record, state, and spouse on file. Two signals are modest: heavy Passport viewers convert somewhat more than their giving predicts, and donors 40 and under convert less.

What This Means for Modeling

  • The 12 month outcome is rare (0.17%), so models are compared on recall, precision, and lift at a list of 1,000, never on accuracy.
  • The bar is high. Prior-year giving alone holds 75% of converters in the top 1,000, and 60% for never-major donors, so the model’s value has to show up as a gain over that ranking, most of all for never-major donors and the longer windows.
  • Giving history is the core of the feature set. Engagement data adds little, so its main role is to be tested, not assumed.
  • Validation has to respect time, spouses, contact, and the funding cut: rolling tests on FY2022 to FY2024, couples in the same fold, contact flags in training only, and the FY2025 cohort kept for final training and one labeled check.

Modeling Recommendations

This section brings the earlier findings together into a plan for the modeling phase. It does not fit a model.

Outcomes and Data

conv_by_window = {
    w: cohorts.filter((pl.col("segment") == "active") & (pl.col("window") == w) & (pl.col("t") >= 2021))
    for w in (1, 3, 5)
}
plan = pl.DataFrame([
    {"outcome": "12 months", "feature_set": "all features",
     "test_cohorts": "FY2022 to FY2024, one at a time", "labeled_check": "FY2025",
     "converters_in_fy2021_on_cohorts": int(conv_by_window[1]["converted"].sum())},
    {"outcome": "within 3 years", "feature_set": "giving history; all features as a secondary check",
     "test_cohorts": "legacy-era cohorts for giving history; FY2021 to FY2022 by grouped cross-validation for all features", "labeled_check": "FY2023 (outcomes through FY2026)",
     "converters_in_fy2021_on_cohorts": int(conv_by_window[3]["converted"].sum())},
    {"outcome": "within 5 years", "feature_set": "giving history only",
     "test_cohorts": "legacy-era cohorts through FY2020", "labeled_check": "FY2021 (outcomes through FY2026)",
     "converters_in_fy2021_on_cohorts": int(conv_by_window[5]["converted"].sum())},
])
show(plan, caption="Outcomes, feature sets, and test cohorts for the modeling phase")
  • 12 month outcome (primary). Becoming major in FY t+1 under the household rule, for active eligible donors. All features are available from FY2021, so this is the outcome the model is judged on.
  • 3 and 5 year outcomes. A strictly time-based test needs training cohorts whose outcomes were known before the test cohort’s prediction date. For the 3 year outcome that means cohorts from FY2019 or earlier when testing FY2022, before solicitation and Passport data exist. The longer windows should therefore be modeled with giving history, which reaches back to FY1999 and, in the baselines section, still ranked 56% of 5 year converters into the top 1,000. A version with all features can be checked by grouped cross-validation on the FY2021 and FY2022 cohorts, reported as secondary. This matches the business problem’s fallback of treating the longer window as a projection when the data spans too few years.
  • Tier. Among predicted converters, the tier reached ($1,200, $2,000, or $5,000 and up). With only 13 converters at $5,000 and up, the top tier will be estimated poorly and should be reported with that caveat.
  • Lapsed segment. With 9 converters in five cohorts, lapsed donors are reported separately with their base rate rather than modeled.

Features

Feature status for the modeling phase
Status Features
Use Prior-year giving, former major status, years given in the last five, years since first gift (with legacy years), legacy-era giving years, change from last year, giving in the two years before, largest gift share of FY t, sustainer status and monthly amount, soft credits before FY t, age at FY t, gender with Unknown as its own level
Test, expected to add little Titles viewed and other Passport measures, recency (with sustainer status), upgrade and additional gifts, soft credits in FY t, solicitation counts, responses, and channels, state, spouse on file
Training only Contacted in FY t, selected but held out in FY t (both off when scoring)
Sensitivity check only Constituent type
Drop Major donor class, annual giving group, sustainer flag, all UofU dollar fields, and anything dated after June 30 of FY t

Giving history is the core of the model. Tree-based models or explicit threshold features should handle the jumps in giving (exact tier amounts, the $600 cluster) better than linear terms in raw dollars. Every feature is built through the shared script so that the same cutoff at June 30 of FY t applies everywhere.

Validation Design

  • Rolling time-based test. For the 12 month outcome, train on all cohorts before the test cohort and test on one cohort at a time: FY2022 (trained on FY2021), FY2023, and FY2024. FY2021 is training only because no earlier cohort has all features.
  • Tuning inside the training years. Hyperparameters are chosen by cross-validation within the training cohorts, grouped by couple so spouses stay in the same fold. The test cohort is never used for tuning.
  • FY2025 cohort. Not used for model selection. After the model is chosen, it is trained on FY2021 to FY2024, tested once on FY2025 as a labeled check across the funding cut, and then retrained on FY2021 to FY2025 for the final list.
  • Class imbalance. With a base rate near 0.15%, accuracy is meaningless. Class weights are fine, but any resampling must happen inside the training folds only.

Measures and Reporting

  • Primary measure: recall at a list of 1,000 per cohort, pooled across the test cohorts, with precision and lift at 1,000 alongside.
  • Secondary measures: average precision over the whole ranking, recall at 1,000 for the longer windows, and a calibration check, since staff will see probabilities.
  • Groups: all eligible donors, never-major donors, and the no-contact pool (contacted donors dropped and held-out donors reweighted), where officer selection is the comparison. The lapsed segment is reported separately.
  • Uncertainty: couple-clustered bootstrap intervals for every rate, recall, and lift.

What Success Looks Like

The model is compared with the baselines on the same test cohorts. The table gives the baseline numbers for FY2022 to FY2024, the three test cohorts in the rolling design.

bars_specs = {k: BASELINES[k] for k in ("prior-year giving", "rule: former major or $500 or more")}
test_scored = scored12.filter(pl.col("t") >= 2022)
bars = pl.concat([
    evaluate(test_scored, bars_specs).with_columns(group=pl.lit("all eligible")),
    evaluate(test_scored.filter(~pl.col("former_major")), bars_specs).with_columns(group=pl.lit("never major")),
]).select("group", "baseline", "recall", "recall_low", "recall_high", "precision", "lift")
bar = {(r["group"], r["baseline"]): r for r in bars.iter_rows(named=True)}
show(bars, pct_cols=["recall", "recall_low", "recall_high", "precision"], caption="Bars the model must clear on the FY2022 to FY2024 test cohorts")

The model succeeds if, on the FY2022 to FY2024 test cohorts, its recall at 1,000 is above the prior-year ranking’s 75.4% for all eligible donors and 59.6% for never-major donors, and it also clears the former major or $500 rule. Because the baseline intervals are about 6.5 points wide on either side, the comparison should be made on the same bootstrap draws (the difference in recall between model and baseline), not by checking whether two separate intervals overlap. A gain among never-major donors matters most, since those are the donors staff are least likely to know already.

Revisions to the Business Problem Statement

The team agreed to revise the business problem statement after the EDA (decision 14). The table lists each change, what the original statement said, and the evidence for the change. A tracked-changes version of the full statement is kept as a separate team document.

Changes to the business problem statement and their evidence
Topic Original statement Revision Evidence
Size of the major donor group About 1% of the donor file and 19% of donor revenue About 0.3% of donors and 8% of individual giving, FY2021 to FY2026 How Rare Major Giving Is
Major donor definition Per individual Per person, except that a couple reaching $1,200 only in combination counts as one major donor; to be confirmed with PBS Utah Household Rule; PBS Classification Fields
Primary success measure At least 25% of converters in the top 10% of the list Recall at a list of 1,000, the cultivation program’s annual capacity, for the 12 month outcome and, as a projection, the 3 to 5 year outcome Baselines
Benchmark Random selection and an RFV baseline Beat the prior-year giving ranking (75% recall at 1,000) and clear a “former major or $500” rule; also report RFV, officer selection, and random selection Baselines
Reporting groups All donors All eligible donors, never-major donors, and donors not contacted by officers; lapsed donors reported separately Conversion Base Rates; Cultivation Program
Giving tiers $1,200, $2,000, $5,000, $10,000, $15,000+ $1,200, $2,000, and $5,000+ (only 13 of the 12 month converters reach $5,000+) Tiers Reached at Conversion
Inputs Giving history, campaign and event participation, UofU engagement and capacity scores, Passport viewing Giving history (including legacy years), soft credits, solicitation history, and Passport viewing. No UofU scores are in the data, and the UofU dollar fields encode PBS giving Snapshot Fields and Leakage
Expected drivers Giving, engagement, and viewing behaviors Mainly giving history and former major status; solicitation and viewing add little once prior-year giving is known Signals From Giving History; Solicitation and Passport Viewing
Validation Time-based validation with a sensitivity test with and without the last year Rolling time-based tests on FY2022 to FY2024, spouses in the same fold, contact flags in training only; the FY2025 cohort used only in final training and reported once as a labeled check Modeling Recommendations; The FY2026 Influx
Longer window Tested if the data spans enough years, otherwise a projection Modeled with giving history and tested on legacy-era cohorts; an all-input 3 year version checked by grouped cross-validation Modeling Recommendations
Risks Leakage, incomplete Passport coverage, the donation influx Adds snapshot-field leakage, the cultivation program’s effect on outcomes, and an unusually large share of first-year donors in the next list Snapshot Fields and Leakage; Cultivation Program; The FY2026 Influx

Points to Confirm With PBS Utah

  • Household rule. The snapshot’s major donor class does not combine spouses, while the team’s rule does. Only one couple is affected in this data, but the rule should be confirmed.
  • Former major donors. They are about half of the converters. If officers already work these donors, the list’s value comes mainly from never-major donors, which is why those results are reported separately.
  • Meaning of contact before program adoption. Contact had a smaller effect before portfolios adopted the program, and it is not clear what contact involved in those years.
  • Missing Passport years. Viewing records rarely carry over from one year to the next, and the data cannot show whether a missing year means no viewing, no linked account, or no consent.

Reproducing This Notebook

import sys
import numpy
import pandas
import plotnine

environment = pl.DataFrame([
    {"component": "Python", "version": sys.version.split()[0]},
    {"component": "polars", "version": pl.__version__},
    {"component": "numpy", "version": numpy.__version__},
    {"component": "pandas", "version": pandas.__version__},
    {"component": "plotnine", "version": plotnine.__version__},
])
show(environment, caption="Software versions used to render this notebook")
  • Data. The repository includes data_cache/, the nine course tables converted to Parquet, and the notebook reads them from there, so the raw CSV files are not needed. To rebuild the cache from the raw release, put the nine CSV files in ../tables relative to this notebook and delete data_cache/; the next render converts them again.
  • Build. All cleaning, panel, cohort, and feature code lives in build_panel.py. The notebook only analyzes what the script builds.
  • Randomness. Every bootstrap uses seed 20261009 and 1,000 resamples, and couples are sorted before resampling, so two renders give identical numbers.
  • Rendering. quarto render pbs_utah_group_eda.qmd. The notebook was rendered with Quarto 1.10, and a full render took two to four minutes on a laptop, most of it in the bootstrap intervals.

    {"step": "Cohorts", "count": "12 month converters, lapsed segment, FY2021 to FY2025", "value": int(lapsed_conv)},
    {"step": "Cohorts", "count": "12 month converters, validation cohorts FY2021 to FY2024", "value": int(active_val["converted"].sum())},
    {"step": "Cohorts", "count": "3 year converters, FY2021 to FY2023", "value": int(conv_by_window[3]["converted"].sum())},
])
show(checks, caption="Counts the R pipeline should reproduce")

Checks on Claims in the Text

Several sentences in this notebook describe a direction or a comparison in words (for example, “an interval that includes 1” or “at the low end of the earlier cohorts”). The chunk below tests each of those claims against the numbers, so a change to the data or the build cannot leave the text saying something the numbers no longer support. The render stops if any check fails.

def includes_one(tbl, feature, level, never=False):
    lo, hi = ("never_low", "never_high") if never else ("ci_low", "ci_high")
    return sig(feature, level, lo, tbl) <= 1 <= sig(feature, level, hi, tbl)

def excludes_one(tbl, feature, level, never=False):
    return not includes_one(tbl, feature, level, never)

others = signals12.filter(pl.col("converters") > 0).filter(
    ~((pl.col("feature") == "Former major donor") & (pl.col("level") == "yes"))
).sort("ratio", descending=True)
higher_than_former = others.filter(pl.col("ratio") > sig("Former major donor", "yes"))

claims = [
    # numbers written out in the Introduction, which comes before any code runs
    ("Introduction: major donors are about 0.3% of donors", round(100 * pooled_share["donors"], 1) == 0.3),
    ("Introduction: major donors give about 8% of individual giving", round(100 * pooled_share["revenue"]) == 8),
    ("Introduction: prior-year ranking holds about 75% at 1,000", round(100 * ba["prior-year giving"]["recall"]) == 75),
    ("Introduction: about half of converters are former major donors", 0.45 <= r12_former["converters"] / r12["converters"] <= 0.55),
    ("Key findings: donors over $500 are under 1% of eligible donor-years", pb["over $500"]["share_of_donors"] < 0.01),
    ("Missing values: Unknown gender is about a fifth of people", 0.18 <= missing.filter(pl.col("field") == "Gender = Unknown")["missing"][0] <= 0.23),
    ("Missing values: about half of eligible donor-years have no Passport record", 0.45 <= no_passport <= 0.55),
    ("Missing values: payment and soft credit tables have no nulls", payment_nulls == 0),
    ("Only 'gave less' has a higher within-band ratio than former major status",
     higher_than_former.select(pl.struct("feature", "level")).to_series().to_list() == [{"feature": "Change from last year", "level": "gave less"}]),
    ("Short histories are about a fifth of expected (all three between 0.15 and 0.25)",
     all(0.15 <= sig(f, l) <= 0.25 for f, l in [("Years since first gift", "1"), ("Years given, last 5", "1 of 5"), ("Change from last year", "no gift last year")])),
    ("Former-major-type signals include 1 among never-major donors",
     all(includes_one(signals12, f, l, True) for f, l in [("Change from last year", "gave less"), ("Giving in the two years before", "$1,200 or more"), ("Soft credit before FY t", "yes")])),
    ("Upgrade gifts and soft credits in FY t: never-major intervals include 1",
     includes_one(signals12, "Upgrade gift in FY t", "yes", True) and includes_one(signals12, "Soft credit in FY t", "yes", True)),
    ("Recency: most recent group below the over-180-day group within bands",
     sig("Days since last gift", "30 or less") < sig("Days since last gift", "over 180")),
    ("Most solicitation intervals include 1",
     np.mean([includes_one(sol_signals, r["feature"], r["level"]) for r in sol_signals.filter(pl.col("converters") > 0).iter_rows(named=True)]) > 0.5),
    ("Viewing record adds nothing (interval includes 1)", includes_one(pv_signals, "Viewing record in FY t", "yes")),
    ("Completion and genre breadth intervals include 1 at every level",
     all(includes_one(pv_signals, r["feature"], r["level"]) and includes_one(pv_signals, r["feature"], r["level"], True)
         for r in pv_signals.filter(pl.col("feature").is_in(["Genres viewed in FY t", "Share of titles watched"])).iter_rows(named=True))),
    ("Heavy viewers exclude 1 for all and never-major donors",
     excludes_one(pv_signals, "Titles viewed in FY t", "over 40") and excludes_one(pv_signals, "Titles viewed in FY t", "over 40", True)),
    ("Age: only the youngest group excludes 1",
     excludes_one(demo_signals, "Age at prediction date", "40 or under")
     and all(includes_one(demo_signals, "Age at prediction date", l) for l in ["41 to 55", "56 to 70", "71 to 85", "over 85"])),
    ("State and spouse intervals include 1",
     includes_one(demo_signals, "Lives in Utah", "yes") and includes_one(demo_signals, "Spouse on file", "yes")),
    ("Held-out donors exclude 1 overall and include 1 for never-major donors",
     excludes_one(cult_signals, "Cultivation group", "selected, held out") and includes_one(cult_signals, "Cultivation group", "selected, held out", True)),
    ("Contact effect interval excludes 0 for all selected donors", eff["all selected donors"]["ci_low"] > 0),
    ("Not-selected FY2025 rate is within 0.005 points of FY2022", abs(gy[(2025, "not selected")] - gy[(2022, "not selected")]) < 0.00005),
    ("FY2025 converter mix shifted in the stated directions",
     cp["FY2025 cohort"]["former_major"] < cp["FY2021 to FY2024 cohorts"]["former_major"]
     and cp["FY2025 cohort"]["gave_over_500_in_fy_t"] < cp["FY2021 to FY2024 cohorts"]["gave_over_500_in_fy_t"]
     and cp["FY2025 cohort"]["reached_2000_or_more"] > cp["FY2021 to FY2024 cohorts"]["reached_2000_or_more"]),
    ("FY2025 prior-year recall is at the low end of the earlier cohorts", rk[2025]["recall_top_1000"] <= rk_before["recall_top_1000"].median()),
    ("RFV recall is below the prior-year interval", ba["RFV score"]["recall"] < ba["prior-year giving"]["recall_low"]),
    ("Former major or $500 matches the prior-year ranking within its interval",
     ba["prior-year giving"]["recall_low"] <= ba["rule: former major or $500 or more"]["recall"] <= ba["prior-year giving"]["recall_high"]),
    ("Officer selection and prior-year ranking intervals overlap",
     nc["officer selection"]["recall_low"] <= nc["prior-year giving"]["recall"] <= nc["officer selection"]["recall_high"]),
    ("Former major or $500 beats the ranking at 3 years and trails at 5 years",
     lt[("within 3 years", "rule: former major or $500 or more")]["recall"] > lt[("within 3 years", "prior-year giving")]["recall"]
     and lt[("within 5 years", "rule: former major or $500 or more")]["recall"] < lt[("within 5 years", "prior-year giving")]["recall"]),
    ("Lifetime UofU is the largest never-major ratio in the notebook",
     sig("Lifetime UofU Fundraising", "over $5,000", "never_ratio", leak_signals)
     > max(t.filter(pl.col("converters") > 0)["never_ratio"].drop_nulls().max() for t in (signals12, sol_signals, pv_signals, demo_signals))),
]
claim_table = pl.DataFrame({"claim": [c for c, _ in claims], "holds": [bool(ok) for _, ok in claims]})
failed = claim_table.filter(~pl.col("holds"))
assert failed.height == 0, f"claims no longer supported: {failed['claim'].to_list()}"

Use of AI Tools

All four team members used AI assistants in their individual EDAs, which this notebook draws on. This group notebook was built with Claude Code (Anthropic), which drafted the shared build script (build_panel.py), the analysis code, the tables and plots, and first drafts of the prose. The team set every definition and decision, including the fifteen agreed decisions and the later refinements, and each section was reviewed before the next one was written.

AI output was not accepted on trust. It was checked in these ways:

  • Reconciliation. Every converter count from the four individual EDAs was rebuilt exactly from the shared panel (Reconciling the Four Individual EDAs).
  • Independent checks of the cleaning. The content-based copy rules were compared with the copy labels in the data, and organization payments were matched to soft credits year by year.
  • Claim checks. The 29 statements in the text that describe a direction or a comparison in words are tested against the numbers in the chunk above, and the render stops if any fails. Several drafted sentences were corrected this way.
  • Reproducibility. Two consecutive renders produce identical numbers, and the cross-check counts give Samantha’s R pipeline a way to confirm the build independently.
  • Reading the output. Every table, plot, and sentence was read against the rendered numbers before a section was accepted, and wording that overstated a result was revised.

Team Contributions

This notebook was an even group effort. All four members completed an individual EDA, compared them together, and agreed on the definitions in the decisions table. Each individual EDA contributed the pieces credited in the Purpose section: Erin’s clustered bootstrap, lapsed segment, threshold baselines, and legacy history indicators; Benjamin’s content-based cleaning rules, snapshot decoding, and FY2026 checks; Kate’s master data dictionary and adoption split; and Samantha’s time-aware eligibility, response timing rule, and audit trail, along with the R pipeline used as a cross-check.
